newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian bank to raise funds for Bakun dam owners.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian bank to raise funds for Bakun dam owners.

text.p: Bank Utama (Malaysia) Bhd said it would raise 840 million ringgit for the eastern Sarawak state government and Sarawak Electricity Supply Corp (Sesco) to fund their purchase of equity in Bakun hydroelectric project.
In a report from Sarawak's capital Kuching, Bernama quoted the bank as saying that the funds would be used by the two customers to subscribe for their 28 percent stake in the 2,400 MW power project.
The giant dam project is being built in Sarawak state on Borneo island at a cost of 15.5 billion ringgit.

The chairman of Utama Banking Group Nik Hashim Nik Yusoff said Bank Utama has also been given the mandate by Tecknoloji Tenaga Perlis Consortium to be the lead arranger and manager of a one billion ringgit syndicated credit facility.
The credit facility would be used to fund the construction of a power plant in Peninsular Malaysia's Perlis state.
"We are also looking forward to playing a meaningful role in the 2.5 billion ringgit Borneo Pulp and Paper project in Bintulu (in Sarawak)," Bernama quoted him as saying.
He was speaking at an underwriting agreement signing ceremony for the initial public offering of Utama Banking Group, which will list on the main board of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange in August.
He also said the group intended to provide a full range of services and act as a one-stop financial centre, with its stockbroking firm to start operations from Miri town by the end of this year.
The group was at an initial stage of negotiating for the takeover of a Kuala Lumpur-based insurance firm, he said.
Utama Banking will issue 683.05 million shares for the listing.

The Bernama report said 33.45 million shares will be restricted for shareholders of Cahya Mata Sarawak Berhad and public issue of 41.15 million shares will be opened for public subscription at three ringgit each.
No other details of the issue were given.
